subject: Agriculture
title: The CGIAR System
description: A fast breakdown of The CGIAR System for builders.

hook.text: CIMMYT and IRRI were just the start. Today, 15 research centers across the world breed crops for the poor.

buildup.text: CGIAR—the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research—coordinates global crop science.

discovery.text: These centers have released thousands of improved varieties—drought-tolerant maize, flood-proof rice, biofortified beans.

twist.text: Funding is shrinking. Donor fatigue and competing priorities threaten the system that feeds millions.

climax.text: CGIAR's work is public. Unlike corporate seeds, their varieties are free for any farmer to grow.

punchline.text: The world's crop insurance system runs on public science—underfunded.

quiz.question: What makes CGIAR crop varieties different from corporate seeds?
options: They're released as public goods, free for any farmer to grow
